_note: THE LOST WALKER. A colonist's mother went out on her morning walk and never came back. He is worried; she is FINE,
sat on a warm rock, a bit turned round. You point her home. The comedy is the gap between the two of them, and nobody
is in danger: a gentle local job, the kind Starfield has none of.
PEN NAME: home-office office/pennames/edie-mallow.json writes HER (her rule: the reader must come away certain she is
fine, and know one concrete thing she likes; humour that never sharpens into a joke). The son is my voice, kept
plain. Overtime is adult, not explicit (his 10-12); Edie's voice applies, not her heat.
ONE THING WORTH BUILDING, Eliza's: after exchange 0 she should SET OFF WALKING toward the colony (a travel package
to the main place's marker). Without it she stays sat on the rock, which is still fine for her, but his idea is that
you point her back. The same question as type 9's allies following the objective; one build answers both.
Voiced lines: no names, no places, roles only. Reward easy: nobody fought anyone.

place._theme: The colony: a lived-in non-hostile site, residents alive.

second._theme: Where she ended up: a natural landmark near the colony (found, held near by the default leash). Somewhere a walker would sit.

prose.name: Rescue: Lost Walker near the <Place> on <Planet>
prose.briefing: A colonist at the <Place> says his mother went out on her morning walk and hasn't come back for lunch.

beats.objective: Talk to the colonist at the <Place>
beats.journal: A colonist at the <Place> says his mother went out on her morning walk and hasn't come back for lunch. I need to go and find her.

person.name: Davit Orrel
hellos: Have you seen an older woman out there? Never mind, I'll explain.

greeting: You heard the call? It's my mum. She goes walking every morning and she's always back for lunch. Today she isn't.

reply: She'll be out there somewhere. If she's hurt, call me. If she's fine, tell her I'm not cross.

exchanges.prompt: Walk the same hills long enough and you try new ones.
reply: She'd never. Actually, she might. She said last week the hills were getting samey.
Never. Twenty years of walks, and she's never once been late for lunch.

exchanges.prompt: What if something's happened to her?
reply: That's the bit I'm trying not to think about. She's tougher than me, but she's not young.

beats.objective: Find the missing walker near the <SecondPlace>
beats.journal: A colonist at the <Place> sent me after his mother, who'd gone out walking that morning and not come back. I found her near the <SecondPlace>, sat on a warm rock and quite all right, just turned round. I pointed her home.

person.name: Maud Orrel
hellos: Oh, hello. Lovely spot for it.

greeting: Hello. I'm sitting down because I like this rock, it holds the sun. Nothing's wrong. I came round the far side for a change, and from here every hill looks like every other hill.

exchanges.prompt: Your son's worried. The colony's that way.
reply: Is it? I'd have sworn it was the other way. Right, I'll head back. He'll have made soup. He always makes soup when he's worried.

exchanges.prompt: A sunny rock and a view. I'd sit a while too.
reply: Wouldn't you? Ground under you, sun on your back. Don't tell my son I said that.
That means he is. It's all right, it's a nice sort of cross.
Not really. I had my flask and the rock was warm. I thought someone would come along eventually, and here you are.

exchanges.prompt: Why do you walk out here?
reply: Because it's quiet and nobody needs anything from me. It's the best hour of my day.

beats._talk: Exchange 0 points her home and ends the Delve. 'He says he's not cross' is set up by her son's closing reply; 'son' by his greeting ('my mum'). Hers is Edie Mallow's register: she is fine, and the greeting carries the one thing she likes (this rock, it holds the sun), so a player who takes exchange 0 first still leaves with it. One clock: she went out THIS morning (Frances Hale, 2026-10-29, rework applied).

broadcast: If anyone's near the colony, we've got someone missing. She went out walking this morning and she's not back for lunch. I know how that sounds, but she's never late.
_speech: The son on the radio and in person (Chris, Charming, Down-to-Earth); his mother is Annie K, one of the two voices heard in game, and calm is exactly her. His ear decides.
